question: Rahul buys a box of pens (listed price of ₹900) with a trade discount of 30%. What is the net price?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The net price is the remaining value after deducting the discount percentage from the listed price.

Net Price = Listed Price × (100% − Discount%)

Net Price = 900 × (100% − 30%)

Net Price = 900 × 70% = 630

**∴ The correct answer is ₹630.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Listed Price (MP) = ₹900

Trade Discount = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Discount Amount = MP × (Discount% ÷ 100)

Net Price = MP − Discount Amount

 
 
 

 
 
 
 MP = ₹900
 
 

 −30% Discount
 
 
 Net Price = ?
 
 Net Price = 900 − 270 = ₹630

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount Amount = 900 × (30 ÷ 100)

⇒ Discount Amount = 900 × 0.30

⇒ Discount Amount = ₹270

⇒ Net Price = 900 − 270

⇒ Net Price = ₹630

**∴ The correct answer is ₹630.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) or Listed Price of an article. Net Price or Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given on an item, the equivalent single discount is given by the formula: (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Profit and Loss Calculation

Unlike discounts which are evaluated on the Marked Price, Profit or Loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP). Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.
